decisions.reason: Memory_slow has the lowest trajectory-level CV NMSE (0.00097), far below the state model, while residual lag correlation suggests omitted history dependence.
decisions.prediction: After irregular input switches, output will retain a history-dependent response for several seconds after the input returns to zero.

mapping.target_relation: Accumulated input history may act as a leaky stored state that predicts output beyond current input and visible state.
mapping.condition_to_check: Under PRBS, test whether past input predicts output after controlling current input and state; no residual effect would falsify this relation.

decisions.reason: Memory_slow remains best on trajectory-level CV, but PRBS error and residual lag correlation leave uncertainty about responses to rapid switches; alternatives validate worse.
decisions.prediction: After alternating input stops, output will retain a history-dependent tail beyond what current input and visible state predict.

mapping.target_relation: A leaky accumulated input history may predict output after input returns to zero, consistent with a stored state.
mapping.condition_to_check: Control for current input and visible state; no predictive effect of past input would falsify this relation.

decisions.reason: Memory_multiscale improves trajectory-level CV over memory_slow (0.001516 vs 0.001723); saturating_memory is only marginally better and uses more coefficients. PRBS errors remain elevated.
decisions.prediction: During irregular switching, fast and slow input histories will produce distinct post-switch responses; after input stops, output will retain a history-dependent tail.

mapping.target_relation: Leaky accumulated input history may carry past influence into output after the input changes.
mapping.condition_to_check: Under PRBS, past input should predict output after controlling current input and visible state; absence of that effect would falsify this relation.
